title: UTNG & Unified Fire Authority- Wildfire Preparation Story
description:
Utah Army National Guard aerial crews prepare for wildfire season with local firefighting teams and the Unified Fire Authority. Video by Sgt. Lark Sine of the 128th Mobile Public Affairs Detachment.

transcript.text: 12 in As summer heats up in Utah ,
so does the risk of wildfires . The
Unified Fire Authority is taking no
chances . Their team based at Camp
Williams completed a critical two-day
training designed to prepare
firefighters for Utah's high risk
summer months . Camp Williams had had
quite a significant fire back in 2010 ,
and we started providing the fire
suppression services for them in 2013 .
On day one , the crews from Camp
Williams and surrounding areas
traversed designated zones
extinguishing simulated fires using
truck mounted hoses , mirroring real
world terrain . There's having to
constantly be aware of the radio track ,
having to constantly be aware of the
adjoining resources and what they're
doing and who's in charge and how that
changes . It really gives everybody a
very good insight into what an actual .
Day two focused on air to ground
coordination . Where firefighters
guided Black Hawk helicopters to
accurately drop water buckets on
designated targets . The whole purpose
of the helicopter is getting the water
bucket right to where they need the
water dumped , basically where trucks
can't get to , so you're , you're
delivering the water right to the
source where the fire is .
Communicating directly with military
aircraft gives these firefighters a
skill set that sets them apart and
prepares them for complex operations .

Every exercise strengthens not only the

This preparation is key to keeping
lives , property , and communities safe .
